messages:
alex: heads-up: after last-night proxy change I see p99 tail regressions for streaming tiny chunks. small writes (<=256B) cause CPU spike and grpc write latency climb.
maria: which change? link to commit?
alex: the proxy patch that removed coalesce hint. repro with many short delta-chunks (chat turns). p95 stable, p99 +30-45ms.
kai: can you share a flame or perf stacks? my hunch is extra memcpy in the socket shim (we saw this pattern when writev fell back).
alex: summary of perf top stacks pasted below:
```
  28%  proxy: socket_send
    -> __sendmsg
    -> do_writev
    -> host_preparse::copy_small_chunk
      -> memcpy
  12%  grpc: stream_flush_coalesce
  10%  tokenizer: tiny-buffer-emit
```
ben: that copy_small_chunk was introduced to normalize http2 frames at edge. I think it's duplicating frame headers for each tiny write.
maria: could batching or kernel selection changes avoid the extra copy? if runtime could present larger logical sequences to the kernel it might eliminate the shim copying.
alex: I prototyped two approaches: (A) reintroduce proxy-level coalesce for small writes; (B) move coalesce into runtime preparse so kernel selection sees larger seqs and we can hint kernels appropriately.
jess: plan sounds like either proxy-level band-aid or runtime-first fix. which performed better in tests?
alex: ran a canary AB (5k streams):
```
patch A (proxy coalesce): p99=120ms (-35ms), cpu +8%
patch B (runtime coalesce+kernel hint): p99=110ms (-45ms), cpu +1%
```
maria: nice. did you check KV cache hit rates? proxy coalesce might change cache keys for prefix frames.
alex: good catch. patch A increased kvcache churn; patch B preserved logical prefixes and improved kv hit rate by ~4%.
kai: any impact on large payloads? we need to ensure we don't regress big writes.
alex: verified up to 64KB, no regressions on the large-path.
ben: patch B is better but touches kernel selection heuristics. rollout plan?
jess: propose: 1) quick rollback of the proxy change if we observe customer impact; 2) land runtime coalesce behind an opt-in feature flag and enable canary; 3) add unit+perf tests focused on many small writes.
alex: opened PR: https://git.redwood/pr/12345. infra-bot started canary (10% us-west-2).
infra-bot: deploy-bot: Canary started for runtime-coalesce feature flag on us-west-2 (10% traffic).
maria: please add microbenchmark for syscall counts and memcpy bytes/sec pre/post.
alex: micro run attached:
```
streams=1000, avg_tokens=12
before: avg_syscalls/stream=18, memcpy_B/s=1.2MB
after: avg_syscalls/stream=5, memcpy_B/s=0.1MB
```
kai: follow-ups: (a) audit other proxy shims that touch frame headers, (b) add kernel-selection metrics to perf dashboard (sequence length distribution), (c) add kv cache key normalization tests.
ben: I'll file tickets and pair with Alex to validate kernel paths.
jess: thanks all. aiming to complete rollout after canary verification. :thumbsup:
alex: will monitor and post updated p99 numbers here in ~1h.
